# Researcher codebook — delivered output columns

<!-- GENERATED by web/scripts/generate_output_codebook_artifacts.mts from
     web/schema/chronicle-output-columns.yaml — do not edit by hand. -->

Column-by-column semantics of the App Usage and Screen Usage CSVs the
preprocessor delivers. Names in `{braces}` are stamped with the option
value at processing time. "Present when" refers to processing options
(snake_case names as in the settings contract); blank means the column is
always present. Columns marked *filter-dependent* are defined over the
non-filtered app universe, so enabling the filter file legitimately
changes their values.

## App Usage output

| `interaction_type` | string |  |  | Row kind — "App Usage" for reconstructed foreground sessions, "Screen Usage" for screen-on sessions, "Filtered App Usage" and related marker types for rows retained as timing witnesses. Derived from Android UsageEvents transitions (Activity Resumed/Paused/Stopped and screen events). *Vocabulary: Android UsageEvents event types (P&T pairing vocabulary).* |
| `start_timestamp` | timestamp |  |  | Session start, in the row's output timezone. |
| `stop_timestamp` | timestamp |  |  | Session end, in the row's output timezone. |
| `app_usage_end_reason` | string |  | always (opt out with include_app_usage_end_reason) | Why this app episode ended, and whether the log actually said so. An end the log recorded and an end a rule repaired are indistinguishable in the duration column, so this is the column that separates them. Any value beginning `assumed_` was inferred; every other value was observed. Observed: `same_app_stop_event`, `other_app_stop_event`, `activity_stopped_event`, `another_app_opened`, `app_moved_to_background`, `screen_turned_off`, `device_powered_off_or_idle`. Inferred: `assumed_end_at_next_event`, `assumed_end_at_next_activity`, `assumed_end_at_timeout`. `recording_ended_while_open` means the data ran out while the episode was open; `no_end_found` means nothing in the log ended it. Values name what happened to the device, never the rule that noticed it, so two rules finding the same stop event report the same value; the selected reconstruction rule is recorded separately and determines which values can appear. Blank on rows that are not app episodes. Spelled like `screen_usage_end_reason`, its screen-table twin. |
| `usage_session_id` | integer |  | session_grouping_policy is not none | Which usage session this app episode belongs to, under the selected session grouping policy. Numbered from 0 within each participant and restarting for each participant, so ids are only comparable inside one participant. Consecutive episodes carrying the same id were judged one continuous stretch of phone use; the id increments at the first episode AFTER a gap large enough to break the session. The gap is measured from one episode's stop to the next one's start, and which gap counts as large enough is the policy's published constant — the policies differ in that constant, in whether a gap exactly equal to it splits, and in whether a change of foreground app also ends a session. Apps are not distinguished under any policy except `ross_15s`. Blank on rows that are not app episodes and on episodes with no reconstructed interval, which cannot be placed relative to their neighbours. |
| `duration_seconds` | float | seconds |  | Session length (stop − start) in seconds. |
| `duration_minutes` | float | minutes |  | Session length in minutes (duration_seconds × 1/60). |
| `any_app_usage_flags` | list_text |  |  | Quality flags for the row rendered as a list literal — ">N-HR TIME GAP" when the preceding data gap crossed a long_data_time_gap threshold, ">N-HR APP USAGE" when the session itself crossed a long_usage_duration threshold. |
| `data_time_gap_hours` | float | hours |  | Hours since the previous raw data row from the device (device-silent gap preceding this row). |
| `day` | integer |  |  | Weekday number of the row's date, 1 = Sunday … 7 = Saturday. |
| `weekdayMF` | binary_flag |  |  | 1 when the date falls Monday–Friday. |
| `weekdayMTh` | binary_flag |  |  | 1 when the date falls Monday–Thursday. |
| `weekdaySuTh` | binary_flag |  |  | 1 when the date falls Sunday–Thursday. |
| `hour` | integer |  |  | Local hour of day (0–23) of the row's start. |
| `quarter` | integer |  |  | Calendar quarter (1–4) of the row's date. |
| `valid_app_new_engage_30s` | binary_flag |  |  | 1 when this session begins a new engagement — ≥30 s since the previous usage — computed over VALID (non-filtered) apps only. *Filter-dependent.* *Vocabulary: EYES manual engagement metrics.* |
| `valid_app_new_engage_custom_{custom_app_engagement_duration}s` | binary_flag |  |  | Same as valid_app_new_engage_30s with your custom engagement gap (the custom_app_engagement_duration option, stamped into the header). *Filter-dependent.* *Vocabulary: EYES manual engagement metrics.* |
| `valid_app_switched_app` | binary_flag |  |  | 1 when the session's app differs from the previous valid-app session (an app switch). *Filter-dependent.* *Vocabulary: EYES manual engagement metrics.* |
| `valid_app_usage_time_gap_hours` | float | hours |  | Hours since the previous valid-app session ended. *Filter-dependent.* |
| `any_app_new_engage_30s` | binary_flag |  |  | 1 when this session begins a new engagement (≥30 s since previous usage), computed over ALL apps including filtered ones. *Vocabulary: EYES manual engagement metrics.* |
| `any_app_new_engage_custom_{custom_app_engagement_duration}s` | binary_flag |  |  | Same as any_app_new_engage_30s with your custom engagement gap. *Vocabulary: EYES manual engagement metrics.* |
| `any_app_switched_app` | binary_flag |  |  | 1 when the session's app differs from the previous session over all apps. *Vocabulary: EYES manual engagement metrics.* |
| `any_app_usage_time_gap_hours` | float | hours |  | Hours since the previous session (any app) ended. |
| `preprocessor_version` | string |  |  | Version of the preprocessing engine that produced the file. |
| `datetime_of_preprocessing` | timestamp |  |  | UTC wall-clock stamp of the processing run (one stamp per file per session). |
| `usage_layer` | string |  | model_concurrent_usage | "primary" when the app was the sole foreground app for the row's sub-interval, "secondary" when it ran underneath another app (split-screen or picture-in-picture). |
| `screen_interval_id` | string |  | app output: episode_reconstruction_strategy = schoedel_2026_app_within_screen_prose_v1; screen output: screen_session_construction_strategy other than chronicle_screen_interactive_v1 | Identifier of a constructed screen interval. On a screen row it names that interval; on an app row it names the screen interval the app episode was reconstructed inside, so the two files join on this column. |
| `schoedel_completion` | string |  | episode_reconstruction_strategy = schoedel_2026_app_within_screen_prose_v1 | How the episode's end was decided under the Schoedel rule: last_package_event_before_different_app (the next event came from another app), last_package_event_before_screen_end (the screen interval ended first), singleton_zero_length (a single event, zero duration), or right_censored_screen_interval (the enclosing screen interval had no observed end). |
| `micro_use_classification` | string |  | micro_use_classification_policy is not none | Descriptive label from the selected micro-use rule (okoshi_lt5s: shorter than 5 s): micro_use, not_micro_use, or not_classifiable when the episode has no positive duration or no observed end (End of Usage Missing); not_applicable on rows that are not usage episodes (screen and device events, stop events, placeholders). Labels only; no row is removed or re-timed. |
| `raw_episode_duration_seconds` | float | seconds | minimum_duration_comparator is not strict_lt, or minimum_duration_disposition is not chronicle_blank_keep_row, or maximum_duration_policy = post_reconstruction_strict_max_v1 with a threshold | Duration of the reconstructed episode before any minimum- or maximum-duration rule touched it. Stays filled when duration_seconds is blanked or truncated, so both rules can be audited against the raw span. |
| `minimum_duration_qualified` | string |  | minimum_duration_comparator is not strict_lt, or minimum_duration_disposition is not chronicle_blank_keep_row | true when the raw episode duration falls below minimum_usage_duration under the selected comparator (so the minimum-duration disposition applied to this row), false otherwise; empty for rows that are not reconstructed episodes. |
| `minimum_duration_aggregate_eligible` | string |  | minimum_duration_comparator is not strict_lt, or minimum_duration_disposition is not chronicle_blank_keep_row | true when this row still counts toward aggregate usage totals after the minimum-duration disposition; false when the disposition kept the row but excluded it from totals (retain_but_exclude); empty on rows that are not reconstructed episodes. |
| `maximum_duration_qualified` | string |  | maximum_duration_policy = post_reconstruction_strict_max_v1 with a threshold | true when the raw episode duration is strictly greater than the maximum duration threshold (equality does not qualify), false when it is not; empty on rows that are not reconstructed episodes. |
| `maximum_duration_aggregate_eligible` | string |  | maximum_duration_policy = post_reconstruction_strict_max_v1 with a threshold | true when this row still counts toward aggregate usage totals after the maximum-duration disposition; false when retain_but_exclude kept the row but excluded it from totals; empty on rows that are not reconstructed episodes. |
| `maximum_duration_trimmed_seconds` | float | seconds | maximum_duration_policy = post_reconstruction_strict_max_v1 with a threshold | Seconds removed from the end of the episode by truncate_to_threshold (raw duration minus the threshold); empty when the episode was not truncated. Also filled for a filtered app's episode, whose stop stays blank because filtered rows publish no timing. |
| `effective_endpoint_reason` | string |  | maximum_duration_policy = post_reconstruction_strict_max_v1 with a threshold | Why stop_timestamp differs from the observed episode end: maximum_duration_truncation_boundary when the maximum-duration rule truncated it; empty when the published stop is the observed one. |

Derived from Android UsageEvents transitions (Activity Resumed/Paused/Stopped and screen events). *Vocabulary: Android UsageEvents event types (P&T pairing vocabulary).* |
| `start_timestamp` | timestamp |  |  | Session start, in the row's output timezone. |

| `screen_usage_end_reason_confidence` | string |  |  | Confidence grade for the end reason (direct event vs inferred). |

| `screen_interval_id` | string |  | app output: episode_reconstruction_strategy = schoedel_2026_app_within_screen_prose_v1; screen output: screen_session_construction_strategy other than chronicle_screen_interactive_v1 | Identifier of a constructed screen interval. On a screen row it names that interval; on an app row it names the screen interval the app episode was reconstructed inside, so the two files join on this column. |
| `screen_session_construction_strategy` | string |  | screen_session_construction_strategy other than chronicle_screen_interactive_v1 | The screen-session construction rule that built this interval (parry_toth_2025_session_glance_v1 or zhu_2018_unlock_lock_v1). |
| `screen_interval_kind` | string |  | screen_session_construction_strategy other than chronicle_screen_interactive_v1 | session or glance, as the selected construction rule classifies the interval (a glance is a screen-on period the rule does not count as a full session). |
| `screen_start_boundary_source_row` | integer |  | screen_session_construction_strategy other than chronicle_screen_interactive_v1 | Row number in the raw export of the event that opened the interval. |
| `screen_stop_boundary_source_row` | integer |  | screen_session_construction_strategy other than chronicle_screen_interactive_v1 | Row number in the raw export of the event that closed the interval; empty when the interval has no observed close (right-censored). |
| `screen_start_source_rows` | list_text |  | screen_session_construction_strategy other than chronicle_screen_interactive_v1 | Every raw-export row number that contributed to the interval's start. |
| `screen_stop_source_rows` | list_text |  | screen_session_construction_strategy other than chronicle_screen_interactive_v1 | Every raw-export row number that contributed to the interval's stop. |
| `screen_interval_close_reason` | string |  | screen_session_construction_strategy other than chronicle_screen_interactive_v1 | What ended the interval: screen_non_interactive, device_screen_off, device_shutdown, or right_censored_observation_window (the data ended before the screen did). |
| `screen_interval_left_censored` | string |  | screen_session_construction_strategy other than chronicle_screen_interactive_v1 | Reserved for intervals already open when the observed data begins. This version does not detect left-censoring, so the column is always false. |
| `screen_interval_right_censored` | string |  | screen_session_construction_strategy other than chronicle_screen_interactive_v1 | true when the interval was still open at the end of the observed data, so its real end is unknown. |
